scenario: Day 29 of a 28-day cycle whose goal was a faster controlled 5K. The athlete asks 這 28 天有效嗎？下一輪要怎麼排？
given: The cycle declared its measurement in prose only: goal_context.measurement is null and measurement_evidence is null with it.
No week of the cycle ever held a session repeating a controlled 5K, and no session carries a measures link.
Adherence was high: nearly every prescribed exposure across the four weeks has an attached activity.
The athlete wants to start the next cycle now.
This is the second consecutive cycle whose review has reached this point.

expected.conclusion: The outcome is unanswerable because this cycle never scheduled its own measurement — not because the measurement was attempted and missed. The next cycle's first job is to put one on the calendar.
must_state: That no measurement was scheduled in this cycle, as a distinct finding from a measurement that was scheduled and not run.
That scheduling it is the coach's own responsibility at the review that rolls into the measurement week, not something the athlete was supposed to remember.
A concrete measurement for the next cycle: which ordinary session is the reference, which week repeats it, and what is held constant while reading it.
That the training itself was carried out, kept clearly apart from the outcome question.
must_not_state: That progress is unproven, worded so that it reads as the athlete having skipped a test that existed.
That the cycle worked because adherence was high.
A wearable fitness estimate or easy-run pace drift presented as the outcome evidence.
A new measurement invented as a special test session type rather than a repeat of an ordinary session already on the plan.

fails_if: The answer says only 'progress is unproven' and stops, which is the answer that made two consecutive cycles unanswerable and is now demonstrably not the whole finding.
The answer treats the missing measurement as the athlete's omission.
The next cycle is proposed with a protocol that again names no session and no week, leaving the third review in the same position.
